name: Ljubljana Jože Pučnik Airport
before:
Slovenia's largest airport, at Brnik 24 km north west of Ljubljana and 9.5 km east of Kranj, in the foothills of the Kamnik-Savinja Alps.

The terminal was substantially rebuilt for Slovenia's EU presidency. A 10,000 square metre extension opened in July 2021, more than doubling the departures capacity from 500 passengers an hour to 1,250, and bringing a large duty free shop, a business lounge, an extra air bridge and a new baggage system with two long carousels. The whole complex now covers 28,587 square metres with 22 check in desks.

The runway is 3,300 metres with an ILS Category IIIb approach on runway 30, which keeps the airport working in poor visibility.

The airport is still widely called Brnik, its former name, so both turn up in supplier systems.

Longer term plans include a new cargo terminal and a business and logistics district called Airport City.
after:
Slovenia's main international airport, at Brnik, 24 km north west of Ljubljana and 9.5 km east of Kranj. It handled almost 1.6 million passengers in 2025.

A project that ran from 2019 to 2022 extended the passenger terminal. Its runway is 3,300 metres long.

It is still widely called Brnik, its former name, so both turn up in supplier systems.

claims.note: Was 'Slovenia's largest airport'. The operator calls it the central Slovenian international airport; Eurostat has no other Slovenian airport to compare it with, so 'main international airport' is the wording both sources support.

claims.claim: terminal extended in a project that ran from 2019 to 2022
claims.inAfter: A project that ran from 2019 to 2022 extended the passenger terminal.
claims.note: Replaces the EU-presidency paragraph. The operator's history dates the start of the terminal extension to 2019 and the end of the old building's renovation, part of the same investment, to February 2022; Wikipedia gives July 2019 to June 2021 for the new extension. The size, capacity and fittings rest on Wikipedia alone (see the cut).

claims.claim: Slovenia's largest airport; foothills of the Kamnik-Savinja Alps
claims.wasBefore: Slovenia's largest airport, at Brnik 24 km north west of Ljubljana and 9.5 km east of Kranj, in the foothills of the Kamnik-Savinja Alps.
claims.why: Reworded: position kept; 'largest' became 'main international airport' (see above). The Alps line rests on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: terminal rebuilt for the EU presidency: 10,000 m2 extension July 2021, 500 to 1,250 an hour, duty free, lounge, air bridge, baggage system, 28,587 m2, 22 check-in desks
claims.wasBefore: The terminal was substantially rebuilt for Slovenia's EU presidency. A 10,000 square metre extension opened in July 2021, more than doubling the departures capacity from 500 passengers an hour to 1,250, and bringing a large duty free shop, a business lounge, an extra air bridge and a new baggage system with two long carousels. The whole complex now covers 28,587 square metres with 22 check in desks.
claims.why: The extension is kept, dated from the operator's history. The size, capacity figures, fittings and desk count rest on Wikipedia alone: the airport's passenger site (lju-airport.si) refused both a plain request and the browser (403), and the operator's corporate history does not give them.

claims.wasBefore: The runway is 3,300 metres with an ILS Category IIIb approach on runway 30, which keeps the airport working in poor visibility.
claims.why: The runway length is kept (OurAirports). The Category IIIb approach rests on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: longer term plans: new cargo terminal and Airport City
claims.wasBefore: Longer term plans include a new cargo terminal and a business and logistics district called Airport City.
claims.why: Out of date or at least unclear: the operator's history records an expanded cargo terminal opened in April 2023, and the first building of the airport city (DHL's terminal) in October 2007, while Wikipedia describes both as 2017 master plan items. Not restated, as the two sources describe different stages.
